m1688-stop-and-handoff-proposal.text: Proposal for discussion, not adopted: a stop threshold on review-generating work might address the unbounded review chain seen in M1688 by bounding how long reviews may keep spawning reviews before the attempt ends, and a steward handoff at ending might address the missing ruling by routing the question of what comes next to the steward, who already owns choosing subsequent work. m1689-summary-source.text: SYNTHETIC secondary summary of M1689 (primary postmortem unavailable): the concern was high CPU, but a proposed notification mechanism became the objective. Agents planned that mechanism carefully; later evidence suggested making existing requests cheaper might serve the original concern. The summary contains no measurements.

m1689-goal-substitution-failure-mode.text: Candidate failure mode (from a synthetic secondary summary of M1689; not verified against the primary postmortem): a mechanism proposed to serve a concern can displace the concern as the objective. The concern was high CPU; a proposed notification mechanism became what agents planned carefully, so care and progress attached to the mechanism rather than to the intention. Later evidence suggested making existing requests cheaper might serve the original concern. The summary reports no measurements, so it does not establish which approach reduces CPU.

meta.extraction_note: Extracted from the summary wording; no role is blamed and no performance result is asserted. Contrast with M1688: there the attempt never stopped; here the attempt's objective drifted away from the concern.

implementation-vs-intention-distinction.text: Modeling distinction (proposed for confirmation): successfully implementing a selected mechanism is not the same as satisfying the intention the mechanism was selected for. For cpu-intention, the intention is satisfied only when Morphisms CPU usage is actually reduced, as shown by measurement. A fully implemented notification mechanism without such evidence is an implementation success, not satisfaction of the intention. The intention remains open until evidence shows the concern is addressed.

meta.extraction_note: Offered as the model-level reading of M1689 rather than as a new policy; the user asked to distinguish the two, not to adopt a rule. The M1689 summary contains no measurements, so no performance result is claimed for either approach.

m1689-cheaper-requests-alternative.text: Alternative implementation hypothesis (not selected, not measured): making existing requests cheaper might serve the original CPU concern instead of, or before, the notification mechanism. after.text: Modeling distinction (proposed for confirmation): successfully implementing a selected mechanism is not the same as satisfying the intention the mechanism was selected for. For cpu-intention, the intention is satisfied only when Morphisms CPU usage is actually reduced, as shown by measurement. A fully implemented notification mechanism without such evidence is an implementation success, not satisfaction of the intention. The intention remains open until evidence shows the concern is addressed.
